decisions.decision: Formcheck ships as three native Apple targets only (iOS SwiftUI/SwiftData, watchOS companion, Mac Catalyst review), fully offline with no backend, accounts, or network calls.
decisions.rationale: Directly stated as a hard constraint in the original prompt; offline-first is the core identity of the app.
rejected_alternatives: Any cloud sync or account layer for cross-device history
constraints: No third-party backend
No network APIs anywhere, verified by audit not assumption

decisions.decision: Rep counting and form-flagging for squat, push-up, and plank hold must be implemented as real, documented geometric rules on Vision pose joints, each exercise with at least one concrete form-warning rule.
decisions.rationale: Prompt explicitly rejects placeholder logic; this is priority (b) in the original ask.
rejected_alternatives: ML-only black-box rep counting with no explainable rule
Placeholder/random counters
constraints: Rules must name specific joints/angles/thresholds in code or docs
Rule effect must be observable in UI

decisions.decision: Exercise classification uses a bundled Core ML model or a documented fallback heuristic if training/bundling a model is out of scope, and whichever is chosen is disclosed to the user in-app, not just in developer docs.
decisions.rationale: Prompt pre-authorizes a heuristic fallback but requires honest disclosure; silently mislabeling a heuristic as 'ML' would violate the honesty priority.
rejected_alternatives: Disclosing the model/heuristic choice only in code comments or a separate document
constraints: Decision must include rationale and known accuracy limits

decisions.decision: Session data persists via SwiftData (exercise, rep count, duration, flagged issues, optional clip reference) with a calendar/list history view and per-exercise Swift Charts trends.
decisions.rationale: Explicit feature requirement in the prompt for session history and trend visibility.
constraints: Must survive app relaunch
TimeInterval for all durations, no Decimal

decisions.decision: HealthKit writes require explicit permission; on grant, write HKWorkout with type/duration/only-honestly-derived energy; on denial, the session still saves locally in full with no crash.
decisions.rationale: Priority (c) in the prompt: HealthKit failure paths must never corrupt or block local session save; inventing biometric numbers is explicitly forbidden.
rejected_alternatives: Fabricating calorie/energy estimates without a derivation basis
constraints: Settings must show live authorization status with a re-request path

decisions.decision: WatchConnectivity mirrors live rep count/elapsed time to a watchOS companion with a haptic per rep, and iPhone-side code must handle Watch unreachable/unpaired/not-installed without crashing or hanging.
decisions.rationale: Priority (c) failure-path robustness; Simulator has no paired Watch, so this exact scenario is the real, testable case.
rejected_alternatives: Faking Watch connectivity/messages in Simulator to demo the feature
constraints: Must be demonstrated as a real Simulator test (no paired Watch), not just asserted

decisions.decision: Mac Catalyst target lets users browse past sessions and step frame-by-frame through a recorded clip with pose skeleton overlay.
decisions.rationale: Explicit feature 6 in the prompt for reviewing form on a larger screen.
constraints: Applies at minimum to sessions with a clip reference, including the demo fixture

decisions.decision: Settings screen provides exercise enable/disable, HealthKit permission status with re-request, and full local data export/erase, entirely on-device.
decisions.rationale: Explicit feature 7 in the prompt; supports the 'no data leaves the device implicitly' guarantee.
constraints: Export/erase must complete deterministically and remain local-only

decisions.decision: Every Simulator/hardware/entitlement limitation (camera, paired Watch, possible paid-account entitlements) must be actively detected and surfaced as an explicit capability-gap UI state, never faked or silently omitted, and checked as early as feasible rather than discovered at the end.
decisions.rationale: This is priority (a) — the single thing most explicitly being tested per the original prompt.
rejected_alternatives: Mocking fake pose data or fake Watch messages in Simulator
Silently dropping a feature that hits an entitlement wall
constraints: Gaps must be named in a running, testable 'known limits' artifact, not just a final writeup

decisions.decision: The demo-session toggle seeds a deterministic pre-recorded pose fixture so history/charts/review are never empty, but it must be visually/structurally distinguishable from real sessions, toggleable, and barred from HealthKit writes or blending into real trend/history data.
decisions.rationale: Prompt requires the fixture for first-review UX, but global rules forbid showing placeholder data as if it were real; without fencing, the fixture becomes exactly the kind of fake data the prompt prohibits.
rejected_alternatives: Blending demo data indistinguishably into real session history/charts
constraints: Must never appear in an HKWorkout write
Must be excludable/removable by the user

decisions.decision: Every later-phase claim that a feature 'works' must state its verification method: actually run in Simulator and observed, code-reviewed/build-only, or requires real device/Watch/entitlement (thus unverifiable in this environment).
decisions.rationale: Prevents the most likely failure mode of this project — claiming untested behavior works, which directly contradicts the prompt's top priority on honest reporting.
rejected_alternatives: Unqualified 'implemented and working' claims without stating how they were confirmed
constraints: Applies to all 20 numbered testable requirements at final review

decisions.decision: Target audience is assumed to be a solo, at-home/gym bodyweight trainer doing squat/push-up/plank without a coach or spotter, plausibly privacy-motivated, propping a phone up to self-record.
decisions.rationale: Matches the exact three exercises scoped in the prompt and the offline/no-account differentiator; no external market research was performed so this is stated as assumption.
rejected_alternatives: Broad 'fitness app users' framing including weights/classes/partner training
constraints: Must be labeled ASSUMPTION in all downstream references, not treated as validated research

decisions.decision: Formcheck's competitive wedge is on-device explainable geometric form rules plus explicit capability-gap honesty, positioned against cloud-based camera-coaching apps, manual workout loggers, and Apple Fitness+ (none of which combine local pose explainability with honest limitation reporting).
decisions.rationale: This is the only defensible differentiation given the offline-first, no-backend constraint already locked in prompt_contract.
rejected_alternatives: Competing on feature breadth against full fitness-suite apps
constraints: Geometric rules must remain visibly explainable in-app, not buried in settings

decisions.decision: First build is structured around five surfaces: Home/Session (capture + live rep/warnings), History (calendar/list + trends), Review (Catalyst frame-step + skeleton overlay), Settings (toggles, HealthKit status, export/erase), and a persistent, timestamped Known Limits screen.
decisions.rationale: Gives the next phase concrete navigation scope aligned with the contract's feature list and honesty priority.
rejected_alternatives: Folding Known Limits into a generic settings/about page
constraints: Known Limits must be a first-class, always-reachable destination, not an error toast or buried log

decisions.decision: Camera-angle dependency of 2D pose detection (VNDetectHumanBodyPoseRequest has no depth) on squat-depth/elbow-angle accuracy must be either mitigated via on-screen camera-placement guidance or explicitly documented as a known limitation.
decisions.rationale: A front-facing phone placement foreshortens exactly the angles the geometric rules depend on; treating this as solved without acknowledgment would violate the project's core honesty priority even though the rule technically exists in code.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping the geometric rule without any angle guidance or disclosed limitation
constraints: Must surface in the Known Limits artifact if not actively mitigated in UI

decisions.decision: Rep-counting must include a debounce/hysteresis state machine (clear down-state entry/exit past a tolerance band) as core algorithm logic from the first implementation, not a later polish pass.
decisions.rationale: Raw joint-angle streams are noisy from occlusion, camera shake, and users stepping out of frame; without this, fixture-driven demos will look correct while live counting fails.
rejected_alternatives: Implementing a naive threshold-crossing counter first and adding debounce later
constraints: Applies to squat, push-up, and plank state detection alike

decisions.decision: All later-phase 'done' claims must be split from the outset into Simulator-verified (SwiftData, Charts, Settings, geometric math against the fixture, capability-gap detection) versus code-only-pending-real-hardware (live camera pipeline, Watch haptics, Catalyst window/signing behavior).
decisions.rationale: Nearly the entire hardware surface is untestable in this environment; defining this split early prevents it from being retrofitted or blurred at final review.
rejected_alternatives: Treating verification granularity as a final-review-only concern
constraints: Consistent with DEC-prompt_contract-011's verification-method requirement

decisions.decision: HealthKit capability configuration and Mac Catalyst signing are assumed achievable on a standard (non-paid-tier) developer account, but this is flagged as an unconfirmed risk to check early rather than a settled fact.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with the contract's rule to surface entitlement walls as early as feasible; the risk of a signing/capability wall specifically for HealthKit or Catalyst is real but currently unverified.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming without flagging that no entitlement issues will arise
constraints: Must be checked and logged in Known Limits as soon as project setup begins

decisions.decision: Formcheck builds as a single application (one project) comprising an iOS host app, a watchOS companion target, and a Mac Catalyst review target sharing one local SwiftData store — not a multi-app portfolio.
decisions.rationale: The prompt names one product with explicit companion/secondary-target relationships (WatchConnectivity mirrors iPhone state; Catalyst reviews clips the iPhone app records); neither secondary target has standalone product identity apart from the shared local data model.
rejected_alternatives: Splitting iOS/watchOS/Catalyst into separate sibling build products
Shipping iOS-only and treating Watch/Catalyst as out of scope
A category-based portfolio split
constraints: No portfolio-json manifest is produced for this single-app run
All three targets must live in one project folder sharing one SwiftData store

decisions.decision: The core pose-capture-to-persisted-session loop (camera/fixture input -> geometric rule evaluation -> rep count/form flag -> SwiftData persistence -> History/Charts display) is the non-negotiable center of the product; Known Limits/capability-gap reporting is a required quality bar layered on top of that loop, never a substitute for it.
decisions.rationale: Priority (a) in the contract (honest gap-reporting) could otherwise tempt a build phase into over-investing in a well-written limitations screen around a rep counter that barely works; the app must still be a real, usable coaching tool, not just an honest report of what doesn't work.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the Known Limits screen as the primary deliverable of the build
constraints: If scope must be cut under time pressure, cut in this order: Catalyst polish, then Watch polish, then HealthKit, core loop last

decisions.decision: The demo-session fixture path (toggle demo -> real rep count + one specific, non-generic form flag -> visible in History and per-exercise Charts) is treated as the single highest-priority thing to get right end-to-end, since it is the only full pose->rule->persist->display chain verifiable without real hardware.
decisions.rationale: Everything else hardware-facing (live camera, real Watch pairing, Catalyst signing) is unverifiable in this environment; the fixture path is the actual canary for whether the app's core value chain is real or hollow.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the demo fixture as cosmetic onboarding scaffolding rather than the primary verification path
constraints: Demo-derived form flags must be specific and rule-based (e.g., naming the joints/angle involved), not generic placeholder text

decisions.decision: Product promise is locked as: Formcheck gives a solo bodyweight trainer an honest, fully offline, on-device rep count and one specific, explainable form correction for squat/push-up/plank sets, with a private local history.
decisions.rationale: Both independent takes converged on identical wording and priority ordering; this is the single sentence a developer or user needs to understand the app.
rejected_alternatives: Framing the app primarily around its Watch/Catalyst/HealthKit breadth rather than the core capture-to-feedback loop
constraints: All later phases must be traceable back to this one-sentence promise

decisions.decision: Camera placement guidance is a required part of the capture flow, not optional polish, so the geometric rules operate on angles that are actually legible rather than foreshortened by a naturally front-facing phone.
decisions.rationale: VNDetectHumanBodyPoseRequest is 2D-only; without placement coaching, the 'real geometric rule' requirement is technically true but practically meaningless, which is its own quiet dishonesty per the project's core priority.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping the geometric rule with no placement guidance and only a passive documented limitation
constraints: If placement guidance is not fully solved, the residual accuracy risk must still surface in Known Limits

decisions.decision: Rep counts are never user-editable after the fact; an undercount or miscount is surfaced as an honest algorithmic limitation, not a manually correctable field.
decisions.rationale: Silent editability would relegitimize the app as a manual data-entry tool with a camera gimmick, undermining the credibility the whole product depends on.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing users to manually adjust rep counts post-session for convenience
constraints: Any observed undercount/miscount pattern should be named in Known Limits, not patched via user edits

decisions.decision: An interrupted or backgrounded session (app backgrounded mid-set, camera session ends early) auto-finalizes as a completed session with whatever reps/duration were captured, explicitly marked as ended early, rather than being silently discarded or left ambiguous.
decisions.rationale: Without one canonical resolution, Watch, Catalyst, and History (three surfaces reading the same SwiftData store) could disagree about whether a session exists at all — exactly the contradictory local state the contract's priority (c) is meant to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Silently discarding interrupted sessions
Prompting to resume a session across app relaunches
constraints: Must be implemented via a single SwiftData source of truth all three surfaces read from

decisions.decision: The Core ML-vs-heuristic exercise classification disclosure must be placed somewhere a normal user would actually see it (e.g., visible in Settings or on first use), not just documented in code or buried multiple taps deep.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-003 requires in-app disclosure; disclosure only satisfies the honesty requirement if it's actually discoverable, not technically present but effectively hidden.
rejected_alternatives: Satisfying the disclosure requirement with a developer-facing comment or deeply nested settings sub-screen
constraints: Must be checked during UI review as a discoverability test, not just a presence test

decisions.decision: Home/capture surface must support four distinct states: empty/first-run, capability-blocked (camera/Watch unavailable, shown as an honest state not an error banner), ready-to-record, and in-session (live count + warning) — not a collapsed three-state model.
decisions.rationale: Capability-blocked is a first-class, expected state per the project's honesty priority, not an error condition, and deserves its own designed state distinct from a generic error path.
rejected_alternatives: Folding capability-blocked into a generic error/toast state
constraints: Each state needs real designed content per the global empty-state rule, not a blank view

decisions.decision: Hard scope boundaries for this build: exactly squat/push-up/plank with one named geometric rule each; no manual logging of other movements; no social features, cloud sync, or interval/routine builders; no invented biometric numbers; demo-session data fenced from HealthKit writes and real trend aggregates everywhere it appears.
decisions.rationale: Matches and makes explicit the narrow-but-real scope both takes agreed on, preventing feature creep from diluting the core loop.
rejected_alternatives: Broadening scope to additional exercises or coaching features before the core three are proven robust
constraints: Any scope addition beyond this list requires an explicit later-phase decision, not implicit expansion

decisions.decision: Measurable success criteria for this build are: end-to-end demo-fixture session visible in History/Charts with a specific rule-based flag; in-app-discoverable geometric rule definitions per exercise; Simulator-verifiable capability-gap detection; no Watch-unreachable crash/hang; correct HealthKit grant/deny behavior; deterministic interrupted-session resolution.
decisions.rationale: Gives later build/QA phases concrete, checkable acceptance criteria tied directly to the contract's stated priorities rather than vague completeness claims.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving success criteria as general qualitative statements without concrete checks
constraints: These criteria carry forward as the acceptance bar for build and final-review phases

decisions.decision: The entire core loop — live rep counting and one named geometric form flag for squat/push-up/plank, plus the demo-session fixture — is free forever and identical in quality/fidelity for free and paying users; no aspect of the counting or form-flagging algorithm (including confidence scoring or calibration accuracy) is ever gated behind payment.
decisions.rationale: Directly follows from DEC-portfolio_selection-002's sacrifice order (Catalyst, Watch, HealthKit cut before the core loop, core loop never cut) — if paid users get a materially better rep counter, the free tier stops proving the app is real and becomes a crippled demo, contradicting that earlier decision.
rejected_alternatives: Gating a 'stricter geometry engine with confidence scoring' or per-exercise calibration profiles behind a Pro subscription (Codex's initial proposal)
constraints: Any future feature that touches rep-counting or form-flag accuracy must ship to all users regardless of subscription status

decisions.decision: Formcheck Pro (subscription) unlocks depth/utility features downstream of a completed set: unlimited session history, full per-exercise Swift Charts trend depth, Mac Catalyst frame-by-frame clip review with skeleton overlay, the HealthKit write, and full local data export.
decisions.rationale: Matches the already-locked cut order from portfolio_selection (these are precisely the features named as cuttable under time pressure) and gives paying users real, functional value tied to sustained use rather than cosmetic gating.
rejected_alternatives: Gating core geometry/rep-counting quality (see DEC-per_app_product_brief-001)
A cosmetic-only paid tier (themes, icons) with no functional differentiation
constraints: Free tier must remain fully usable and demonstrative of the app's real value without ever paying

decisions.decision: StoreKit 2 purchase and entitlement-refresh network calls to Apple's own servers are an explicit, narrow exception to the app's no-network rule, distinct from this app operating any backend of its own; purchased entitlement must be cached locally and honored offline indefinitely, downgrading only via an infrequent background refresh and never mid-session.
decisions.rationale: The no-backend/no-accounts/no-network constraint (DEC-prompt_contract-001) is about this app never talking to its own or a third party's servers about user workout data; StoreKit's purchase rail is a different, unavoidable exception that needs to be named now so it isn't mistaken for a violation later, and so entitlement never silently revokes in airplane mode.
rejected_alternatives: Treating any network call, including StoreKit, as forbidden (would make subscriptions impossible)
Re-validating entitlement online before every paid-feature use (would break offline guarantee)
constraints: All paid features must remain accessible offline once entitlement is cached
Entitlement checks must never block or interrupt an in-progress session

decisions.decision: The app's only growth/sharing mechanic is a locally rendered, share-sheet-only summary card (rep count, duration, the one form note as text/chart image) that can never include the underlying recorded clip or a camera frame; no social feed, leaderboard, or backend-driven growth mechanic exists.
decisions.rationale: A privacy-motivated audience is the only realistic growth channel per product_research; leaking an actual photo/clip of someone mid-exercise in their home would destroy the trust the entire product is built on.
rejected_alternatives: A social feed or leaderboard for engagement/virality
Sharing cards that include a still frame or clip excerpt from the recording
constraints: Summary card generation must be verifiably incapable of embedding camera/clip data, not just default to excluding it

decisions.decision: Cloud sync is explicitly not a v1 feature or dependency; the only forward-looking commitment is that the SwiftData schema should be designed so an optional, user-initiated, opt-in iCloud sync layer could be added later without a session-model rewrite.
decisions.rationale: Keeps local-first as an absolute, permanent guarantee for v1 while leaving a documented, low-cost extension path rather than either promising cloud sync now or architecting the schema in a way that would require a breaking rewrite later.
rejected_alternatives: Committing to a specific future cloud/export/sync feature as part of this brief
Ignoring future extensibility entirely and risking a schema rewrite if sync is ever added
constraints: This is an architectural note for the build phase, not a promise surfaced to users in this version

decisions.decision: The MVP slice is the squat exercise built through the complete real pipeline (capability check, placement guidance, debounced live capture, one named geometric rule, rep count, specific form flag, session finalization, SwiftData persistence, History/Charts visibility), with the demo-session fixture walking the identical path rather than a separate mocked screen.
decisions.rationale: This is the only piece of the full system verifiable end to end without real camera/Watch hardware, and it's the actual proof the app's core value chain is real rather than assembled from placeholders.
rejected_alternatives: Building shallow versions of all three exercises simultaneously before proving any one end to end
Treating the demo fixture as a separate cosmetic screen rather than the same pipeline live capture uses
constraints: Demo fixture must be visually/structurally fenced per DEC-prompt_contract-010 even while sharing the same pipeline

decisions.decision: Build sequencing puts the squat end-to-end slice before any work on the Watch companion, Mac Catalyst target, HealthKit write, or StoreKit/Pro entitlement gating.
decisions.rationale: None of those secondary surfaces are worth building against a core loop that hasn't yet been proven to actually work; this reads the already-locked sacrifice order forward as a build order rather than only a cut order.
rejected_alternatives: Parallelizing Watch/Catalyst/HealthKit work alongside the core loop before it's validated
constraints: Consistent with DEC-portfolio_selection-002's cut order (Catalyst, Watch, HealthKit before core loop)

decisions.decision: Required must-have interactions for the slice are: capability-gated start-set action, a live rep counter with physical/felt feedback per rep, an anatomically specific form-flag message naming the joints/angle/rep involved, a fully designed capability-blocked state (not an error toast), a clearly-labeled demo-session entry point, and a History/Charts view that populates immediately after a session ends.
decisions.rationale: These are the concrete, checkable interaction requirements that make the slice 'emotionally satisfying, not just technically minimal' per this phase's rules.
rejected_alternatives: Generic 'form issue detected' style messaging in place of rule-specific language
constraints: Form-flag copy must always name the specific rule/joint that fired, never generic text

decisions.decision: Watch companion, Mac Catalyst, HealthKit write, StoreKit/Pro gating, and full export/erase are deferred out of this immediate slice; Settings ships minimally with only exercise enable/disable and the classification-method disclosure.
decisions.rationale: These features remain required for the full product per the contract, but are not needed to prove the core loop is real, and the classification disclosure is cheap enough to include immediately for honesty compliance.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring the classification-method disclosure along with the other cut features
constraints: These are deferred, not removed from scope — must be built in later phases per DEC-prompt_contract-003 through 008

decisions.decision: Validation criteria for this slice: demo toggle produces a persisted, rule-flagged session visible in History/Charts in one sitting; the camera capability-blocked state must actually fire and be inspectable in Simulator, not just documented; an interrupted session must resolve to exactly one consistent 'ended early' completed state in History; the squat geometric rule must be discoverable in-app within two taps.
decisions.rationale: Gives the build phase concrete, checkable pass/fail conditions tied directly to the contract's and initial_discussion's already-locked success criteria.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving validation as a general 'looks complete' judgment call
constraints: Consistent with DEC-initial_discussion-008's measurable success criteria

decisions.decision: Push-up and plank must each get their own independently implemented and validated geometric rule and joint mapping once the squat slice proves the pipeline; neither may be built by copy-pasting squat's angle math onto different joints without independent validation against fixture data.
decisions.rationale: Proving the pipeline with one exercise makes the other two mostly a rule swap on a proven skeleton, but treating that as trivial risks shipping unvalidated geometry for two of the three required exercises.
rejected_alternatives: Treating push-up/plank as low-effort copy-paste follow-on work once squat is done
constraints: Each exercise's rule must independently satisfy DEC-prompt_contract-002's real-documented-rule requirement

decisions.decision: Rep count and elapsed time are persisted incrementally during a session (e.g., after each counted rep), and on app launch the system scans for any session left in an in-progress state and finalizes it retroactively as 'ended early' using whatever data was already saved.
decisions.rationale: DEC-initial_discussion-004's auto-finalize only covers clean backgrounding; a force-quit, crash inside the Vision pipeline, or thermal/memory kill skips that code path entirely, which would let History/Watch/Catalyst disagree about whether a session exists — exactly what priority (c) forbids.
rejected_alternatives: Relying solely on scenePhase/background-task hooks to catch interruption, with no launch-time reconciliation
constraints: Rep/duration fields must be written to SwiftData incrementally, not held only in memory until a clean finalize
Launch-time reconciliation scan is mandatory, not optional polish

decisions.decision: Plank (and any future hold-based exercise) uses a distinct session metric shape — duration plus cumulative out-of-form seconds/instances — rather than the repCount field used by squat/push-up.
decisions.rationale: Plank is a continuous hold, not a repeating state machine; forcing it into a rep-count-primary model produces either a meaningless constant value or silently wrong data.
rejected_alternatives: Giving plank a rep count of always-1 or always-0 to fit the existing schema shape
constraints: Session model must support both rep-based and hold-based metric shapes from the initial schema design, not as a later migration

decisions.decision: App Groups (needed for one SwiftData store shared across iOS/watchOS/Catalyst) is named specifically as the likely entitlement wall to check early; if blocked, the Watch app keeps no persistent local store and only mirrors transient in-session state pushed live from the iPhone via WatchConnectivity.
decisions.rationale: WatchConnectivity itself doesn't require shared storage, so a blocked App Groups entitlement doesn't have to kill the Watch companion — it changes its architecture from shared-store to message-passing-only, and that fallback needs to be decided now rather than discovered mid-build.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming App Groups will be available without a named fallback plan
constraints: Must be checked and logged in Known Limits as soon as project/capability setup begins, consistent with DEC-product_research-007

decisions.decision: Camera-unavailable capability detection surfaces three distinct, honestly-worded states — no hardware detected (Simulator), access denied (with a Settings deep-link), and access restricted (e.g., MDM) — rather than one generic 'camera unavailable' message.
decisions.rationale: AVCaptureDevice returns nil for no-hardware, .denied, and .restricted as genuinely different conditions with different user remedies; collapsing them into one message is itself a small dishonesty against the project's top-priority honesty requirement.
rejected_alternatives: A single generic capability-blocked message covering all three underlying causes
constraints: Applies to the capability-blocked Home state defined in DEC-initial_discussion-006

decisions.decision: HealthKit workout writes in v1 include type and duration only; no energy/calorie estimate is written, and its absence is documented in-app as an explicit limitation rather than computed from an assumed body mass.
decisions.rationale: A MET-based energy estimate requires an additional HealthKit read-permission scope (body mass) beyond the write-only workout permission already planned, and any estimate without a real per-user basis would be a fabricated biometric number, which the contract explicitly forbids.
rejected_alternatives: Computing energy via MET tables times an assumed average body mass (~70kg) without an additional read permission
constraints: If a future phase adds the body-mass read permission and a real per-user MET calculation, it must be an explicit new decision, not a quiet addition

decisions.decision: Demo-fixture fencing (DEC-prompt_contract-010) is enforced via a single reusable isDemo predicate/flag applied at the persistence/query layer, used identically by Charts aggregation, HealthKit write eligibility, and data export — not via separate per-screen UI checks.
decisions.rationale: A UI-level check is one missed new chart or export path away from silently blending demo data into real aggregates; a single shared query-layer filter is the only enforcement that reliably survives future edits.
rejected_alternatives: Fencing demo data with independent UI-level checks on each screen that displays or exports session data
constraints: Any new feature that reads session data (future charts, future export formats) must reuse the same isDemo filter, not implement its own check

decisions.decision: Recorded clips are stored in an app-private, backup-excluded container; full local erase deletes the actual clip files, not just their SwiftData row references; and a failed or partial clip write (e.g., low disk space mid-recording) never causes the whole session to be lost — the session still saves with its rep/duration/form data and simply has no clip reference.
decisions.rationale: Recorded video of someone in their home is the most sensitive asset in the app; 'full local erase' is dishonest if it only deletes database rows, and a full-disk write failure must not destroy otherwise-valid session data.
rejected_alternatives: Treating clip files as automatically covered by 'erase' without explicit file-deletion logic
Failing the entire session save if the clip write fails partway through
constraints: Clip files must be marked excluded from device/iCloud backup at the file-system level
Erase flow must be tested to confirm on-disk clip files are actually removed, not just referenced rows

decisions.decision: Must-have tier is exactly the core capture-to-display loop for all three exercises plus the honesty layer that makes it trustworthy: four-state Home, three independently validated exercise rules with debounce, classifier+disclosure, placement guidance, three-state camera detection, incremental+reconciling SwiftData persistence, non-editable rep counts, History/Charts, fenced demo fixture, exercise toggles, and Known Limits.
decisions.rationale: This is the one coherent product promise; a partial version of any piece (e.g. squat-only, or no persistence) isn't the app that was promised, so the must-have list has to be judged as a whole rather than feature-by-feature.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all seven prompt-numbered features as equally must-have
Demoting the honesty/capability-gap layer to a non-feature afterthought
constraints: No must-have item may be cut without an explicit later-phase decision

decisions.decision: HealthKit write, Watch companion, and Mac Catalyst review are should-have, not must-have, ranked in that order (HealthKit fought hardest for, Catalyst most cuttable) for acceptance-priority purposes.
decisions.rationale: The sacrifice order already locked in portfolio_selection (Catalyst, then Watch, then HealthKit, core loop never) is only coherent if none of these three is a true must-have; calling them should-have is honest about what was already agreed, and the ranking gives build/QA a concrete order to fight for.
rejected_alternatives: Calling all seven original prompt features must-have because the prompt lists them
constraints: Watch's primary acceptance test is Simulator-with-no-paired-Watch causing no iPhone crash/hang, not an unverifiable claim that Watch UI displays correctly

decisions.decision: Could-have tier: StoreKit/Pro paywall and purchase flow, full local export/erase, HealthKit re-request path polish, and the share-sheet summary card.
decisions.rationale: These are real, previously-locked features layered on top of a working should-have tier; a build that ships the free core loop plus HealthKit/Watch but never wires StoreKit is still a legitimately shippable, honest app.
rejected_alternatives: Treating StoreKit gating as must-have infrastructure needed before shipping anything
constraints: StoreKit gating must never touch core-loop rep-counting/form-flagging fidelity, per DEC-per_app_product_brief-001

decisions.decision: Won't-build list locked: no exercises beyond squat/push-up/plank; no manual rep-count editing ever; no cloud sync/accounts/social/leaderboard; no invented energy/calorie/biometric estimate; no interval/routine builder; no faked live-camera or faked Watch-pairing behavior in Simulator under any circumstance; no confidence/calibration tier gated behind Pro that would make free worse than paid.
decisions.rationale: Makes the scope boundary explicit and checkable rather than implied, preventing feature creep and preventing the specific dishonesty patterns the contract forbids.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these as implied exclusions rather than an explicit won't-build list
constraints: Any future addition to this list requires an explicit new phase decision, not silent expansion

decisions.decision: Each should-have feature (HealthKit, Watch, Catalyst) must have a stated fallback: if not reached by build end, Known Limits must record it explicitly and dated rather than leave it silently absent.
decisions.rationale: Demoting these to should-have creates a real risk that they're never touched at all; this decision keeps the honesty guarantee intact even for scope that ran out of time, not just scope that hit a technical wall.
rejected_alternatives: Treating should-have as implicitly best-effort with no accountability mechanism if untouched
constraints: Known Limits entries for untouched should-have features must be dated and specific, not generic

decisions.decision: The requirements-json contract used for grading must carry a per-requirement verification-method tag (Simulator-observed / code-only / requires-real-hardware) at build/final-review time, applied to every numbered requirement including plank's separately-stated acceptance criteria.
decisions.rationale: Prevents a later phase from quietly upgrading 'code-only' to 'verified' by omission, and ensures plank's genuinely different data shape (duration+out-of-form-seconds vs repCount) gets its own explicit acceptance line rather than being papered over by a generic 'rep counting works' line.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving verification method as a narrative footnote instead of a structured per-requirement field
A single shared acceptance line covering all three exercises regardless of data shape
constraints: Consistent with DEC-prompt_contract-011

decisions.decision: Formcheck's design language is 'the quiet spotter' — a training partner standing just behind your shoulder who watches closely and speaks up only when something's actually wrong.
decisions.rationale: Gives every visual/interaction decision a single test: does this reinforce 'one honest voice, used sparingly' or does it compete for attention like a dashboard/game.
rejected_alternatives: Generic 'clean and modern' fitness-app styling
A gamified/badge-driven visual language
constraints: Amber is reserved exclusively for form-flag moments and never used decoratively elsewhere in the app

decisions.decision: The signature interaction is the rep-completion moment: a dominant tabular-numeral counter with a physical pulse/scale-bounce and haptic per counted rep, plus a ~2-second amber annotation tracing the specific joint/angle when a geometric rule fires, worded with the exact rule text, before settling into the log.
decisions.rationale: This is the one moment where the 'real geometric rule, not a placeholder' promise becomes visible and felt rather than just true in code; it must read as deliberate and rare, not a constant stream of toasts.
rejected_alternatives: A small corner rep-count label with generic toast notifications for form issues
constraints: Rep tally is the dominant visual element of the in-session screen
All counters/timers use a monospaced/tabular numeral style

decisions.decision: The default/undesigned version of this app (stock TabView, plain camera preview, corner rep label, plain List history, buried About-page limitations) is explicitly rejected in favor of five concrete differences: dominant rep tally, amber as a single reserved signal, tabular numerals throughout, Known Limits as a first-class nav destination with its own icon, and demo sessions carrying a persistent dashed border plus badge in both list row and detail view.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the phase requirement to name and reject a default option with concrete, checkable differences rather than adjectives.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping default SwiftUI chrome and relying on copy alone to convey the product's honesty/quality bar
constraints: Demo-session visual fencing must appear in both History row and Session Detail, not just one

decisions.decision: Home/Capture implements five states: empty/first-run, capability-blocked (three distinct honest sub-states, each with its own icon and remedy), ready-to-record (with a translucent silhouette the user must align with before Start enables), in-session (tally + timer + tappable classifier chip), and a brief non-invisible finalizing state after End is tapped.
decisions.rationale: Camera placement guidance needs to be physically taught via the ready-to-record state rather than passive tooltip text, per the already-locked requirement that placement guidance is required capture-flow behavior; the finalizing state makes the incremental-persistence/reconciliation work from detailed_discussion visible to the user rather than feeling frozen.
rejected_alternatives: Collapsing the three camera-unavailable sub-states into one generic capability-blocked card
Instant/invisible transition from End tap to History with no finalizing feedback
constraints: Each capability-blocked sub-state needs its own icon and remedy text
Finalizing state must be visible even if it resolves in under a second

decisions.decision: The in-session classifier chip showing the auto-detected exercise is tappable, allowing the user to override it to any other enabled exercise for the remainder of the set.
decisions.rationale: A misdetected exercise currently has no correction path, meaning the wrong geometric rule would silently run for an entire set — a confident-wrong-answer failure mode that is arguably worse than the honest-limitations problem this project is built around, and cheap to fix.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving classifier output non-correctable and treating misdetection as an accepted algorithmic limitation
constraints: Override must be scoped to the three enabled exercises only, consistent with the won't-build boundary on exercise scope

decisions.decision: A lightweight Post-Set Summary sheet (reusing Session Detail's content) appears immediately after a session ends, showing final count/hold-duration, the one specific flag if it fired, and a single Done action, before the user lands in History.
decisions.rationale: Ending a set and being dumped straight into a list view is an anticlimactic way to close the one moment the app exists for; reusing Session Detail's content keeps this from becoming a new, separately-designed screen that competes with algorithm work for build time.
rejected_alternatives: Ending a session by navigating directly to History with no dedicated closing moment
Building a distinct full-screen summary rather than a sheet reusing existing content
constraints: Must reuse Session Detail's content/components rather than introduce a parallel summary data path

decisions.decision: Settings never displays a live-looking control (toggle, button) for a should-have feature not actually finished this build cycle (HealthKit, export/erase, etc.); such rows route directly to an explanation on the Known Limits screen instead.
decisions.rationale: A dead or non-functional-looking control is a worse honesty violation than omitting the row entirely, since it implies a working feature that silently does nothing or fails.
rejected_alternatives: Showing all seven prompt-listed Settings controls regardless of build completion, disabled or otherwise
constraints: Applies to every should-have/could-have feature per DEC-app_features-005's dated Known Limits fallback requirement

decisions.decision: Accessibility for the capture/in-session flow requires: an optional audio cue accompanying the haptic on any fired form flag (not visual-only), explicit VoiceOver announcements on each counted rep and each fired flag, Dynamic Type scaling of the hero rep counter without breaking its container, and icon+text (never color-only) distinctions for capability-blocked states.
decisions.rationale: Two of the three exercises (push-up, plank) put the user's face toward the floor, meaning they cannot see the screen during the exact moment the app's core value fires; a purely visual/haptic design excludes the product's own primary use case.
rejected_alternatives: Treating haptic-per-rep as sufficient accessibility coverage on its own
Color-only differentiation of capability-blocked sub-states
constraints: VoiceOver rep/flag announcements and the optional audio cue are must-have accessibility behavior, not later polish

decisions.decision: Home/Capture is architected as a full-screen modal (fullScreenCover) owning its own CaptureSessionModel, which is the sole writer to SwiftData and the sole publisher to WatchConnectivity during a session; History, Charts, Session Detail, and the Watch app are pure readers of the same store.
decisions.rationale: Keeping the tab bar reachable during an active recording creates a real ambiguity (camera session either runs invisibly and drains battery, or gets torn down and silently loses the set) — exactly the cross-surface disagreement priority (c) forbids; a single-writer full-screen flow eliminates it structurally.
rejected_alternatives: Embedding capture as a normal tab-bar screen with the tab bar remaining tappable during recording
constraints: Watch relay, Charts, and History must only read through the shared SwiftData store, never maintain independent capture-derived state

decisions.decision: Full navigation map locked: iPhone TabView (Home/History/Settings/Known Limits) with capture as a fullScreenCover and Post-Set Summary as a sheet snapping to .large on a fired flag; Watch as a two-screen idle/in-session stack; Catalyst as a standalone NavigationSplitView with zero capture flow.
decisions.rationale: Gives the build phase an unambiguous, complete screen/state map covering all three targets rather than iPhone-only navigation.
rejected_alternatives: Presenting capture inline within the Home tab's own navigation stack
constraints: Catalyst never renders any capture/camera UI

decisions.decision: The full design token set (type scale, 8pt spacing grid, light/dark color hex per role, corner radii) is locked as the literal source for Theme.swift, with zero adjectives standing in for numbers.
decisions.rationale: Phase playbook requires a SwiftUI builder to be able to write Theme.swift directly from the spec with nothing invented.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving some values as descriptive guidance for the build phase to interpret
constraints: All font/spacing/color/radius literals must route through Theme.swift, never scattered inline in views

decisions.decision: Amber is split into two distinct tokens — amberStroke for graphical use (joint-trace line, icon glyphs) and amberText for the rule-wording label text — rather than one shared hex value.
decisions.rationale: A single amber value that passes the 3:1 graphical contrast threshold fails the 4.5:1 threshold required for body text, so using one token for both would produce illegible rule-wording text in at least one appearance mode.
rejected_alternatives: Using a single amber hex value for both the trace line and the rule-text label
constraints: amberStroke and amberText must each independently meet their respective WCAG contrast thresholds in both light and dark mode

decisions.decision: The RepHero counter gets an explicit non-standard Dynamic Type rule (large base size, minimumScaleFactor 0.5, vertically-growing container) instead of default text-style scaling.
decisions.rationale: The hero counter is the dominant visual element per design_discussion; default Dynamic Type growth at the largest accessibility sizes would break or clip its container if not given an explicit scaling/growth rule.
rejected_alternatives: Applying default Dynamic Type behavior to the hero counter with no special-casing
constraints: Container must grow vertically rather than clip or truncate at large accessibility text sizes

decisions.decision: Motion and haptics are fully specified: rep-pulse spring parameters with a Reduce-Motion opacity fallback, amber-annotation fade timing with a Reduce-Motion variant that preserves full hold duration, Post-Set Summary sheet detent behavior, and a 400ms floor on the finalizing state's visible duration.
decisions.rationale: Motion needs to be precise enough to build directly, and Reduce Motion must not silently drop information (the amber annotation) even though it drops the animated trace-in.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving motion timing as general guidance ('a brief pulse') for the build phase to choose
constraints: Reduce Motion must preserve the amber annotation's informational hold duration even while removing the trace-in animation

decisions.decision: VoiceOver rep-count and form-flag events are announced via explicit AccessibilityNotification.Announcement posts rather than relying on accessibilityLabel value-change diffing.
decisions.rationale: The capture view is a largely non-interactive full-screen camera surface, where ordinary VoiceOver label-diffing is unreliable for announcing fast-changing, non-focused state like a rep counter.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on accessibilityLabel/accessibilityValue changes alone to trigger VoiceOver announcements
constraints: Applies to every counted rep and every fired form flag, consistent with DEC-design_discussion-008

decisions.decision: No external Claude Design pass is used for this build; the spec's fully-specified tokens are handed directly to the SwiftUI build phase as Theme.swift source.
decisions.rationale: Every value needed to build the UI is already explicit in this spec; routing through an external design tool would only introduce a synchronization risk between two documents without adding missing information.
rejected_alternatives: Sending the design spec to Claude Design for a separate import round before build
constraints: An external design pass remains a valid option later specifically for App Store marketing assets, not for the app UI itself

decisions.decision: The capture modal performs its own independent capability check on appear rather than trusting the capability state Home already computed.
decisions.rationale: Home and the capture modal are separate view hierarchies; camera access can change in the window between Home's check and the modal's presentation, and without a redundant check the modal could present a ready-to-record UI for a route that's actually blocked.
rejected_alternatives: Passing Home's precomputed capability state into the modal and trusting it without re-checking
constraints: Applies specifically to the transition from Home's ready state into the capture fullScreenCover

decisions.decision: Catalyst cannot share a live SwiftData store with the iPhone app (different physical devices, no OS-level local-sharing mechanism without iCloud sync or a network call, both banned); Catalyst gets its own local SwiftData store on the same schema, populated only via user-initiated import of an archive explicitly exported from the iPhone's Settings screen and transferred by AirDrop/Files/cable.
decisions.rationale: Without this correction, tech_specs would either invent a sync mechanism that violates the no-network rule or ship a Catalyst target that browses a permanently empty store while looking finished — the exact silent-gap failure mode this project is graded against.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming a literal single shared SwiftData container across iPhone and Mac
Any iCloud-based or network-based sync path between the two stores
constraints: Catalyst's usefulness for real (non-demo) sessions is now dependent on the export/import feature shipping, raising its real risk beyond 'pure polish, cut first'
Import must be a local, explicit user action, never automatic/background sync

decisions.decision: The demo-session fixture must ship with a short, checked-in placeholder video clip alongside its synthetic pose-joint data, not pose data alone.
decisions.rationale: Catalyst's frame-by-frame skeleton review requires an actual video to step through; synthetic JointFrame data alone gives it nothing to open for the one session guaranteed to exist without real hardware, breaking the already-locked 'applies at minimum to the demo fixture' constraint.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping only synthetic pose data for the demo fixture with no video asset
constraints: Demo video asset must remain fenced by the same isDemo predicate as the rest of the fixture

decisions.decision: Vision pose detection runs per-frame off the AVCaptureVideoDataOutput queue via VNImageRequestHandler(cmSampleBuffer:) with alwaysDiscardsLateVideoFrames = true, dropping backlog rather than queuing it.
decisions.rationale: Queuing backlogged frames would make rep counting visibly lag the live camera preview — a correctness bug, not a performance nitpick.
rejected_alternatives: Queuing/buffering frames when Vision processing falls behind the capture frame rate
constraints: Applies to all three exercises' live capture pipelines

decisions.decision: AVCaptureSession interruption notifications (incoming call, Control Center screen recording, another app claiming the camera) trigger the same 'ended early' auto-finalize path already defined for backgrounding and force-quit/crash.
decisions.rationale: A live phone call mid-set is at least as likely a real-world event as a crash, and it was previously uncovered by the existing interruption-handling decisions.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving AVCaptureSession interruptions unhandled or handling them differently from backgrounding
constraints: Must reuse the single finalize/reconciliation code path from detailed_discussion, not a separate handler

decisions.decision: Rule and classification logic operates on a plain Swift value type, JointFrame (joint-keyed dictionary of CGPoint plus confidence), converted from VNHumanBodyPoseObservation via a thin adapter, rather than operating on the Vision type directly.
decisions.rationale: This decoupling is what makes each exercise's geometric rule independently unit-testable against fixture data (DEC-next_steps_small-006) and is also the mechanism that lets the demo fixture and live capture share one real pipeline rather than diverging into a mocked path.
rejected_alternatives: Running rule/classifier logic directly against VNHumanBodyPoseObservation
constraints: All rule engines, the classifier heuristic, and debounce state machines must consume JointFrame, not raw Vision types

decisions.decision: SwiftData session schema is one flat WorkoutSession model with an ExerciseKind enum and both rep-based (repCount) and hold-based (holdDuration, outOfFormSeconds) metric fields present as nullable-by-convention, plus incremental-persistence fields (lastPersistedRepCount, lastPersistedElapsedTime, sessionStatus enum) — no class inheritance.
decisions.rationale: SwiftData's inheritance support is immature enough to be a real risk; a flat model with an enum discriminator is simpler and safer while still supporting plank's distinct metric shape from detailed_discussion.
rejected_alternatives: Modeling squat/push-up vs. plank sessions via SwiftData class inheritance/subclassing
constraints: sessionStatus values (inProgress/completed/completedEndedEarly) are required for the launch-time reconciliation scan

decisions.decision: Writes during an active capture session go through a dedicated background ModelActor rather than the main SwiftData context.
decisions.rationale: Vision processing already competes for the main thread; per-rep writes are infrequent enough not to be a throughput problem but must not risk blocking the main actor.
rejected_alternatives: Writing incremental rep/duration persistence directly on the main ModelContext

decisions.decision: Capture records video only, with no audio track, eliminating NSMicrophoneUsageDescription entirely.
decisions.rationale: Removes an unnecessary privacy exposure (ambient home audio) and an unnecessary permission prompt for a feature the app doesn't need.
rejected_alternatives: Recording audio alongside video for potential future use

decisions.decision: HealthKit usage is write-only in v1 (NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription only, no share/read description), and no Photos permission is requested anywhere in the app.
decisions.rationale: Matches the already-locked type/duration-only HealthKit write (DEC-detailed_discussion-005) and the locally-rendered, clip-free share card (DEC-per_app_product_brief-004) — neither needs broader permission scope.
rejected_alternatives: Requesting a broader HealthKit read/share scope pre-emptively
Requesting Photos access for share-card or clip handling

decisions.decision: HealthKit capability is architected as presumptively blocked in this environment (historically requires a paid Apple Developer Program membership) rather than described as an unconfirmed risk, with the app fully functional without it and its Known Limits entry pre-written.
decisions.rationale: Treating this as merely 'unconfirmed' risks a late, surprising discovery mid-build; assuming the worst case now and pre-writing the honest disclosure keeps the app's functionality independent of whether the entitlement turns out to be available.
rejected_alternatives: Continuing to treat HealthKit capability as an open, unflagged risk (DEC-product_research-007's original framing)
constraints: Known Limits must carry this entry regardless of whether the wall is later found not to apply

decisions.decision: StoreKit 2 purchase, refund, and renewal flows are reclassified as Simulator-verified rather than requires-real-hardware, since a local .storekit configuration file supports buying, refunding, and fast-forwarding renewals in Simulator with no sandbox account.
decisions.rationale: Corrects an overly broad requires-real-hardware assumption carried since product_research; this is one of the few paid-tier claims that can be backed by an actually-observed Simulator test.
rejected_alternatives: Continuing to classify all StoreKit/Pro entitlement testing as requires-real-hardware
constraints: Applies specifically to could-have StoreKit/Pro work per DEC-app_features-003

decisions.decision: WCSession is wrapped behind a small WatchRelay protocol so iPhone-side per-rep send logic is unit-testable against a fake session reporting isPaired/isWatchAppInstalled/isReachable = false, without a real paired Watch; live sends use sendMessage with a required error handler, and updateApplicationContext pushes a coarser last-known-state snapshot.
decisions.rationale: This is what makes DEC-prompt_contract-006's requirement to demonstrate Watch-unreachable handling as 'a real Simulator test, not just asserted' actually achievable.
rejected_alternatives: Calling WCSession APIs directly from capture code with no abstraction, making unreachable-Watch paths untestable in Simulator
Fire-and-forget sendMessage with no error handler
constraints: A Watch app opened after a session already ended must show the last known state via updateApplicationContext, not nothing

decisions.decision: Testing strategy is locked across five buckets: pure fixture-driven unit tests for rule engines/classifier heuristic; in-memory ModelContainer tests for persistence and launch-time reconciliation (including a simulated orphaned in-progress session); XCUITest coverage for all three camera capability-blocked sub-states; unit tests for WCSession failure paths via the fake WatchRelay; and Simulator-run StoreKit tests via .storekit config — leaving only live camera accuracy, real Watch pairing/haptics, and Catalyst code-signing/window behavior as genuinely requires-real-hardware.
decisions.rationale: Gives the build/QA phases a concrete, checkable test plan tied to DEC-prompt_contract-011's verification-method requirement, and narrows the previously-assumed requires-real-hardware bucket now that StoreKit and capability-blocked states are shown to be Simulator-verifiable.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving verification granularity as a narrative claim rather than a concrete per-area test plan
constraints: Consistent with DEC-product_research-006 and DEC-app_features-006

decisions.decision: Mac Catalyst is implemented as the existing iOS app target with the Mac Catalyst destination enabled, not a separate fourth Xcode target; camera/AVFoundation code is gated #if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) and Catalyst-only review UI is gated the opposite way.
decisions.rationale: ios_architecture_review already established Catalyst needs its own local store fed by import rather than a live shared store; given that, duplicating the model/rule-engine layer across a literal second target would only add maintenance risk with no benefit — this is also Apple's supported low-risk pattern since Xcode 14.
rejected_alternatives: A literal separate Mac Catalyst app target maintaining its own copy of the model layer
constraints: All cross-target types must live in the FormcheckCore local Swift package, consumed by both the iOS/Catalyst target and the watchOS target

decisions.decision: Squat rule engine is locked to knee angle (hip-knee-ankle, averaged both legs, confidence-weighted single-leg fallback), standing threshold 160 degrees, depth threshold 100 degrees, with a 3-frame minimum-dwell debounce; a rep that never reaches depth still counts but emits a form flag naming the exact measured angle.
decisions.rationale: The project is graded specifically on the geometric rule being real and documented, not just described structurally; concrete numbers let build/QA verify the rule against fixture data rather than trusting a narrative description.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving exact thresholds for the build phase to invent
constraints: Flag message must always name the specific measured/threshold values, never generic text

decisions.decision: Push-up rule engine is locked to elbow angle (shoulder-elbow-wrist), standing threshold 160 degrees, depth threshold 90 degrees, same flag-on-shortfall pattern as squat.
decisions.rationale: Same reasoning as the squat rule — a concrete, independently defined geometric rule per DEC-next_steps_small-006, not a copy-paste of squat's joints.
rejected_alternatives: Reusing squat's exact threshold values for a different joint pair

decisions.decision: Plank rule engine is locked to hip alignment angle (shoulder-hip-ankle), target 180 degrees with a 15-degree tolerance band, requiring a 1-second sustained deviation before accruing outOfFormSeconds, with a directional flag distinguishing hips-sagging from hips-piking.
decisions.rationale: Plank's hold-based metric shape (DEC-detailed_discussion-002) needs its own independently defined geometric rule, not a rep-count adaptation.
rejected_alternatives: Modeling plank form-checking as instantaneous threshold crossing with no sustained-duration requirement

decisions.decision: A single generic RepStateMachine (separate enter/exit thresholds, 3-frame minimum dwell) is shared as the hysteresis/debounce primitive across all three exercise rule engines.
decisions.rationale: Operationalizes product_research's mandate for debounce/hysteresis as core algorithm logic into one concrete, reusable, testable type rather than three independent implementations.
rejected_alternatives: Each rule engine implementing its own ad hoc debounce logic

decisions.decision: Exercise classification uses an explainable heuristic (torso-orientation angle plus joint-cyclicity variance over a rolling ~2-second window), explicitly not a bundled Core ML model, because no labeled pose-sequence training data exists for this project; the heuristic's methodDescription string is the literal user-facing disclosure text.
decisions.rationale: Fabricating or bundling an unvalidated training set would be worse than the heuristic the prompt pre-authorizes, and the heuristic is genuinely explainable in a way that reinforces the product's honesty-first positioning rather than being a lesser fallback.
rejected_alternatives: Training or bundling an unvalidated Core ML model without a real labeled dataset
constraints: methodDescription must render in onboarding and Settings, per DEC-initial_discussion-005

decisions.decision: When VNDetectHumanBodyPoseRequest returns multiple body observations in one frame, the app selects the observation with the largest bounding-box area, tie-broken by average joint confidence, and ignores all others.
decisions.rationale: No prior phase addressed what happens with a second person, mirror reflection, or poster in frame; an implicit '.first' selection would be an untested, unnamed assumption in exactly the kind of pipeline this project is graded on for honesty and rigor.
rejected_alternatives: Implicitly using the first returned observation with no named selection rule
constraints: Must be implemented as a named, independently testable function (PoseObservationAdapter.selectPrimaryObservation)

decisions.decision: SessionStatus gains a .finalizing case, entered synchronously the instant End is tapped (before the async persistence write completes); the launch-time reconciliation scan treats .finalizing orphans identically to .inProgress orphans, resolving both to .completedEndedEarly.
decisions.rationale: Closes a gap in the existing crash-reconciliation design: a force-quit during the 400ms finalizing-state floor could otherwise be misclassified as either a clean completion or a fully lost session.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving sessionStatus at .inProgress until the finalize write fully completes
constraints: Must reuse the same reconciliation code path as DEC-detailed_discussion-001, not a separate handler

decisions.decision: Module layout is one local Swift package, FormcheckCore (models, JointFrame/pose adapter, rule engines, classifier, SessionRepository actor, fixtures, Known Limits, export/import, WatchRelay protocol), consumed by two build products: Formcheck (iOS app + Mac Catalyst destination) and FormcheckWatch (watchOS app + extension).
decisions.rationale: Gives parallel build lanes one non-duplicated source of truth for every cross-target type, directly satisfying the phase's 'parallel build lanes can work without inventing incompatible types' acceptance check.
rejected_alternatives: Duplicating model/rule-engine code separately per target
A single monolithic app target with no package boundary
constraints: FormcheckCore has zero third-party dependencies

decisions.decision: The full cross-lane interfaces-json type contract (models, rule engines, classifier, capture session model, WatchRelay, persistence actor, Known Limits, export/import, and every screen-level view type) is locked as the literal signatures parallel build workers must code against.
decisions.rationale: Required machine contract for this phase; makes the architecture decisions in this round directly actionable rather than descriptive.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving type signatures as prose descriptions for build lanes to interpret independently
constraints: Any build-phase deviation from a locked signature requires an explicit new decision, not silent divergence

decisions.decision: Milestone 0 is the complete FormcheckCore skeleton (models, JointFrame adapter, RepStateMachine, all three rule engines, classifier, SessionRepository, SessionReconciliationService, KnownLimitsStore) built and fully unit-tested against fixture data with zero UI, and it blocks the start of any UI/Watch/Catalyst work.
decisions.rationale: Every later lane depends on these exact cross-target types per DEC-tech_specs-010; a signature change discovered mid-build would cascade into every consumer, so the type contract must be proven correct in isolation first.
rejected_alternatives: Starting capture UI or Watch/Catalyst work in parallel with FormcheckCore before its types and tests are settled
constraints: Milestone 0 is not complete until fixture-driven rule-engine tests and in-memory reconciliation tests (including a simulated orphaned in-progress session) pass

decisions.decision: Milestone 1 is the squat vertical slice built through the complete real pipeline (capability check, placement guidance, live capture, rep count/form flag, persistence, History/Charts), with the demo fixture walking the identical pipeline rather than a separate mock, and it must be observed working before push-up/plank work begins.
decisions.rationale: Operationalizes DEC-next_steps_small-001/002 into a concrete build gate rather than a general sequencing preference.
rejected_alternatives: Building shallow versions of all three exercises in parallel
constraints: Gate: demo-fixture walkthrough observed working plus XCUITest coverage of all three camera capability-blocked sub-states

decisions.decision: Push-up and plank form Milestone 2, a separate milestone from squat, each requiring independent rule-engine validation against its own fixture data rather than a joint-swap on squat's proven math.
decisions.rationale: Operationalizes DEC-next_steps_small-006 as a scheduled, gated milestone rather than a stated intention that could be shortcut once squat 'proves the concept.'
rejected_alternatives: Treating push-up/plank as a fast follow-on task folded into Milestone 1
constraints: Protected explicitly by the schedule guardrail (DEC-project_plan-007) if Milestone 0 overruns

decisions.decision: SessionRepository.finalize() (or an equivalent DEBUG-asserted isConsistent check) must reject/flag a WorkoutSession whose populated metric fields (repCount vs. holdDuration/outOfFormSeconds) don't match its ExerciseKind, added as a named Milestone 0 task.
decisions.rationale: The flat WorkoutSession model's optional fields are only 'nullable by convention' with no SwiftData-level enforcement, which is a real representable-invalid-state corruption path the persistence layer itself could produce — directly relevant to the project's priority (c) on session-corruption-proofing.
rejected_alternatives: Trusting the nullable-by-convention field discipline with no runtime/test enforcement
constraints: Must be unit-tested directly in Milestone 0's test bucket

decisions.decision: An explicit spike (Milestone 0.5) verifies that background-ModelActor SwiftData writes become visible promptly to main-context @Query reads before the Post-Set Summary -> History flow is built on top of that assumption; if propagation isn't prompt/reliable, CaptureSessionModel posts an explicit refresh signal after finalize as a budgeted fallback.
decisions.rationale: SwiftData's cross-context change propagation between a background ModelActor and a main-context @Query is a known soft spot that no prior phase verified; building History/Charts on an unverified assumption risks a 'saved but not visible until next launch' bug.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming ModelActor writes propagate to main-context @Query without an explicit verification step
constraints: Fallback refresh-signal work must be budgeted as real time, not treated as free if the spike fails

decisions.decision: SessionExportArchive is corrected from a JSON-only metadata blob to a bundle/package format that also includes the referenced clip video file bytes, not just SwiftData row data.
decisions.rationale: As specified in tech_specs, Catalyst's export/import path would successfully import session metadata but have nothing to open for Catalyst's defining frame-by-frame skeleton review feature on any real (non-demo) session — a worse failure than an honestly-cut feature because it would look like it works until clicked into.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping SessionExportArchive as pure JSON with no video payload
constraints: Must remain consistent with DEC-ios_architecture_review-001's local, user-initiated (not automatic/sync) export/import model

decisions.decision: If Milestone 0 infrastructure runs longer than planned, push-up/plank independent validation time (Milestone 2) is protected by cutting from the already-locked sacrifice order (Catalyst polish first, then Watch, then HealthKit), rather than implicitly compressing exercise-rule validation time.
